headline: France Is Heavy Favorites, But Morocco's Path to the Final Is Wider Than You'd Think
body: The model gives France a commanding 68.7% chance to win this quarterfinal and a 35.5% shot at the final — numbers that match the conventional narrative of a dominant side. What casual fans may underestimate is Morocco's structural resilience: the simulation still lands them in the final in 10.2% of all 10,000 runs, a non-trivial ceiling for a side rated 222 Elo points below their opponents. That gap between perception and probability is exactly where Morocco's 3.6% title chance quietly lives.

headline: Spain's Path Looks Even Cleaner Than the Scoreline Suggests
body: The model gives Spain a 69.3% chance of winning this quarterfinal, but the more telling number is what happens next: Spain reaches the final in 42.1% of all 10,000 simulations and claims the title in 25.3%. Casual fans may see Belgium as a dangerous dark horse, yet their title probability sits at just 4.9% — the Elo gap of 216 points between these sides (2177 vs. 1961) leaves little room for romantic narratives.

headline: England Dominate on Paper, But Norway Are No Quarter-Final Fodder
body: Conventional wisdom says England, with a 104-point Elo advantage, should cruise past Norway — and the model largely agrees, giving them a 60.7% chance to advance. What might surprise casual fans is how often Norway flips the script: the simulation has them reaching the semifinal in 39.3% of 10,000 runs and lifting the trophy in 5.8%. Norway aren't here to make up the numbers — they're here to make England uncomfortable.

headline: Argentina Are Firm Favorites, But Switzerland's Path to Glory Is Wider Than It Looks
body: The model gives Argentina a commanding 68.2% chance to advance past Switzerland, consistent with their Elo rating of 2156 — one of the tournament's highest. What casual fans may overlook is that Switzerland still converts their quarterfinal appearance into a final appearance 13.2% of the time across 10,000 simulations, a figure that reflects their structural resilience deep in tournaments. Argentina's 22.6% title probability makes them one of the simulation's strongest contenders, but Switzerland's 4.8% championship share is not the statistical rounding error their underdog status might suggest.
